cds.text: Measure and compare objects by length, capacity and mass using uniform informal units, and smaller units when more accuracy is needed
Identify which metric units measure everyday items; use known measurements to make estimates
Interpret unmarked and partial units when measuring length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature, using scaled and digital instruments
Identify common uses of halves, quarters and eighths with shapes, objects and events, and represent them
Measure and compare objects using familiar metric units of length, mass and capacity, and instruments with labelled markings
Recognise ways to measure and approximate perimeter and area of shapes and enclosed spaces using formal and informal units
Identify dates and find the number of days between events using calendars
Use the relationship between formal time units (days, hours, minutes, seconds) to estimate and compare event durations
Solve problems involving duration, including am and pm situations and conversions between time units
Recognise and read time on an analog clock to the hour, half-hour and quarter-hour
Describe the relationship between hours and minutes on analog and digital clocks; read time to the nearest minute
Estimate and compare angles using names (acute, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution) and relate them to a right angle
Identify, describe and show quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns in everyday situations
Identify angles as measures of turn and compare them with right angles in everyday situations
Recognise relationships between dollars and cents and represent money values in different ways
